record.paper_title: New Open Problems Related to Old Conjectures by Helleseth
record.original_question: Let s be an invertible exponent over a finite field of odd characteristic, and assume s ≉ 1. Must 2 always occur as a differential multiplicity of s? That is, for every such invertible exponent, does there always exist some v for which the number N(1, v) of solutions to x + y = 1 and x^s + y^s = v equals 2?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 6.9 (optimist). Let s ≉ 1 be an exponent over a finite field of odd characteristic. If s is invertible, then 2 is a differential multiplicity.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{F}_q$ be a finite field of odd characteristic $p$ with $q = p^n$ elements. For an integer $s$ with $\gcd(s, q-1) = 1$ (so that $x \mapsto x^s$ is a permutation of $\mathbb{F}_q$), and for $v \in \mathbb{F}_q$, define
$$N(1, v) = \#\{(x, y) \in \mathbb{F}_q \times \mathbb{F}_q : x + y = 1,\ x^s + y^s = v\}.$$
A nonnegative integer $m$ is called a differential multiplicity of $s$ if there exists some $v \in \mathbb{F}_q$ with $N(1, v) = m$.

Prove or disprove: for every odd prime power $q$ and every $s$ with $\gcd(s, q-1) = 1$ and $s \not\equiv 1 \pmod{q-1}$, the value $2$ is a differential multiplicity of $s$; that is, there exists $v \in \mathbb{F}_q$ with $N(1, v) = 2$.
artifact.category_tag: Differential spectra of power functions over finite fields
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture (an "optimist" conjecture about 2 always being a differential multiplicity for invertible exponents in odd characteristic) is stated as an open problem in the context of Helleseth-related conjectures. Web searches for its resolution return only related work on differential spectra of specific power mappings (e.g., Niho exponents, Ness–Helleseth function), with no source establishing or refuting the general statement. Status appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: On a Conjecture of Helleseth
status_evidence.snippet: Discussion of Helleseth-type conjectures on Weil sums and exponents over finite fields.
status_evidence.claim: Helleseth-type conjectures on exponents over finite fields are an active area; no resolution of the differential-multiplicity-2 conjecture is reported.

status_evidence.title: A note on the differential spectrum of the Ness–Helleseth function
status_evidence.snippet: Recent (2024) work computing the differential spectrum of a particular power mapping in odd characteristic.
status_evidence.claim: Recent research determines differential spectra in special cases but does not settle the general 'optimist' conjecture.
